text:
maya: Heads up — turned on packed kernels for the 4096-seq BatchingBench run and saw ~+7% latency regression vs baseline on A100. attaching nsys flame and the short timeline.

sam: ugh. is this end-to-end or just the fused-attn op microbench?

maya: microbench + e2e on batch sizes 1/2/4. the regression shows up only for long seq (>=2048) and only when packed kernels + bias+rope inline are enabled. short seqs are fine.

priya: can you paste the nsys stack? L2 or dram blowup maybe.

maya: paste from flame: 
```
GPU memcpy HtoD: 0.4ms
fused_attention_packed_kernel: 3.8ms
-> shared_mem_bank_conflict: spikes at ~0.8ms
L2: read throughput +15% vs baseline
DRAM: same
```

maya: also saw a lot of small mem ops around KV lookup/prefetch region.

leo: that smells like L2 thrash from interleaved prefetch ordering across heads. if packing changed access stride, L2 lines might be ping-ponging.

sam: can we try grouping prefetch by head-block to make accesses more linear? low effort toggle in kernel.

maya: tried two quick flips: (1) head-major prefetch ordering and (2) disable bias+rope inline. results on 4k seq: baseline packed kernels = +7% ; (1) head-major prefetch => +2% ; (2) disable bias+rope => +4% ; both changes => -1% (slightly faster).

priya: nice. so bias+rope inline exacerbates the bad stride pattern. maybe it changes register pressure and forces different spilling/lds layout.

leo: another angle: check shared mem usage per block. if we bumped shared mem a bit (due to packing epilogue temp buffers), we could drop occupancy and get less L2 prefetch overlap.

maya: current kernel config: 
```
// before
shared_mem_per_block = 48KB
registers_per_thread = 96
block_threads = 256

// packed change
shared_mem_per_block = 60KB // epilogue temporaries
registers_per_thread = 112
```

maya: occupancy drops from 80% -> 52% with that change.

perf-bot: microbench summary: 4096 seq, bs=1, packed=on, bias+rope=on => 7.1% latency regression; occupancy correlated.

sam: ok actionable list: 1) reduce shared mem temp usage (maya) 2) try head-major prefetch ordering (priya) 3) add `__ldg`/coalesced prefetch hints and test L2 hit rate (leo) 4) add occupancy and l2-miss counters to CI microbench (perf-bot).

maya: I'm on (1) and will run a small sweep: shrink epilogue buffer and pack into registers where safe. will post numbers.

priya: I'll prototype the prefetch reordering and a version that batches prefetches by page to avoid interleaving with paged-KV. quick perf plan: nsight `--metrics l2_hit_rate,gld_transactions,shared_store_transactions`.

leo: if the register pressure from bias+rope inline is the culprit we should add a compile-time toggle and keep default conservative. also file a perf regression ticket.

maya: created draft perf regression issue: https://redwood.internal/p/infra/PR-5821 — put the reproducer and initial traces.

sam: great. also let's label the benchmark as "long-seq-packed" in perf dashboard so it doesn't get lost.

perf-bot: noted. will add to nightly microbench and include occupancy/L2 charts.

maya: preliminary follow-ups: after shaving 8KB shared mem and applying head-major prefetch, I got parity with baseline on 4k seq (+0.2%). will run full CI.

leo: awesome. if that holds, we'll upstream the prefetch ordering and add the bias+rope inline toggle behind a flag.

priya: i'll push the prefetch PoC to a branch and tag maya for validation.

maya: thanks team — leaving traces / commands in the issue. :thumbsup:
